text:
sanjay (sales): Quick sync on Rivermark POC. They route on-prem through an AWS Transit Gateway into a VPC and want to reach our service via AWS PrivateLink. Requirements: preserve SNI for hostname routing, have a small set of egress IPs to allowlist on their corporate firewall, and minimal DNS changes. Any gotchas?

maria (sre-se): AWS PrivateLink exposes an interface endpoint in the customer's VPC (private IP). From on-prem -> TGW -> VPC reaches that IP. SNI is preserved as long as TLS is passthrough (no TLS termination on the egress device). If their Palo Alto or proxy terminates TLS, SNI won't reach our side.

olivia (netops): On egress IPs: for our Private (dedicated) customers we can allocate a static EIP/NAT pool per-customer or advertise a narrow set of egress IPs per-region for hosted PrivateLink. Recommend they allowlist our published egress IPs rather than every possible ephemeral IP.

kevin (customer): Our netsec will only accept a list of <=5 IPs. Can you provide that? Also, do we need to open management/control ports or just 443?

olivia (netops): Primary ports = TCP/443 only for inference and control plane callbacks. No additional UDP or high-range ports required. We'll provide an artifact with the 4 IPs for us-east-1 that you can drop into their firewall policy. Want me to attach it to the ticket?

kevin (customer): Yes please. Also they asked for an example Palo Alto security rule or cli snippet so they can hand it to their NetSec team.

olivia (netops): Palo Alto snippet (PAN-OS CLI) below, replace <REDWOOD_IPS> with the list we provide:

```
configure
set rulebase security rules Allow-Redwood from trust to untrust source any destination <REDWOOD_IPS> service service-tcp-443 application ssl action allow
commit
```

olivia (netops): If they use policy objects instead of inline IPs create an address-object group containing the EIPs and reference that in the rule.

ashley (solutions): Also include an HAProxy/edge example in case they want an on-prem TCP passthrough proxy that routes by SNI without terminating TLS. This helps customers using appliances that can't do ssl_preread.

olivia (netops): HAProxy tcp SNI routing example (minimal):

```
# haproxy.cfg (tcp mode, SNI-based routing)
frontend fe_tls
  bind *:443
  mode tcp
  tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
  tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 }

  use_backend bk_service1 if { req_ssl_sni -i service1.rwood-example.com }
  use_backend bk_service2 if { req_ssl_sni -i service2.rwood-example.com }
  default_backend bk_default

backend bk_service1
  mode tcp
  server s1 10.0.10.5:443

backend bk_service2
  mode tcp
  server s2 10.0.10.6:443
```

olivia (netops): That preserves SNI and performs L4 routing without TLS termination. Works well with TGW egress flows.

maria (sre-se): DNS: PrivateLink typically wants private DNS so the public hostname resolves to the interface endpoint IP inside the VPC. Options for them:
- Create an AWS PrivateHostedZone and associate with VPCs.
- Push an explicit A record into their on-prem DNS resolvers (if allowed).
- For quick POC, test with /etc/hosts on a bastion VM.

kevin (customer): Their DJs (DNS team) will push a split-horizon entry for the service name in the VPC resolver, but they wanted to avoid touching many resolvers. Rule of thumb?

maria (sre-se): For low friction: do the hosts file test, then the AWS PrivateHostedZone for scale. If they truly cannot change DNS, we can provide explicit IPs for the POC, but that's fragile if we change endpoints. We'll flag that as POC-only.

ashley (solutions): Any concerns about mutual TLS? They asked if we support client certs.

maria (sre-se): We can support mTLS on PrivateLink, but it requires cert distribution and test certificates from both sides. It's an advanced configuration in our Private offering and will add time to the POC (we need certs uploaded to our control plane and an extra validation step). If NetSec requires mTLS we should scope it separately.

olivia (netops): Enterprise blocker note: if their firewall or TGW NAT rewrites source IPs and they insist on source-IP pinning to a particular application instance, we need to coordinate NAT design. Preferred model is: customer allowlists our egress EIPs. If they want to identify originating hosts, they can implement mapping in their side NAT.

infra-bot: Ticket #POC-5102 created and assigned to @olivia. Attachments to include: egress-ip-artifact-us-east-1.csv, PaloAlto-snippet.txt, haproxy-example.cfg, PrivateDNS-howto.md.

sanjay (sales): Thanks folks. @kevin I'll attach the ticket link and the artifacts once infra-bot uploads. Follow-up: NetSec meeting tomorrow 14:00 ET.

kevin (customer): Great, we'll be there. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
